title: Thermochemical processes (mechanisms?) of biochar production under KUNTAN kiln and NABERTHERM furnace. Effects of technologies on organic fractions
content:
Abstract

Non-conventional biochar production to solve environmental challenges has met skepticism due to a sustpected gulf in quality between conventional and local biochar production systems. However no experimental evidence exists to compare biochars from both systems. Based on the premise that pyrolysis is thesame under both production systems inspite of differences in system parameters, this experiment sets out to investigate and compare the characteristics of two biochars produced from the Kuntan kiln and a Naberthem furnace. Three feedstocks, viz. rice husk (RH), peanut hull (PH), and sawdust (SD) were thermochemically decomposed at five average temperatures to produce five types of biochar as RH480K, RH560K, PH440K, PH540K, and SD463.5K. Using the same temperatures (attached as subscripts) a Naberthem furnace was used to carbonize thesame feedstocks into RH480F, RH560F, PH440F, PH540F, and SD463.5F biochars. Results from the characterization of the biochar types indicate that furnace- biochars had higher recalcitrance, higher aromatic carbon (aryl-C), fewer functional groups and low amounts of Nitrogen and Hydrogen. In contrast, the Kuntan kiln biochars retained more functional groups,have lower carbon content and higher levels of Nitrogen and Hydrogen and lower aromaticity. Results also confirmed that both technologies deployed the same reaction paths during pyrolysis. The furnace biochar types are best suited for C sequestration and long-term C storage, while the Kuntan biochar types can improve soil CEC and water holding capacity in addition to improving other soil properties biochar is known for. Similar reaction paths and properties of both biochar types confirm similar pyrolytic process in the two technologies and confirms the premise. A more in-depth study with other advanced spectrometric methods will throw more light on biomass transformation under these two technologies.
